content.title: About
content.content: Dried shrimp are marine crustaceans that have been cleaned, cooked and then dehydrated at low temperature. They have an intense sea aroma, firm texture and a bright red color. Dried shrimp are widely used in Asian cuisine as a flavoring ingredient in salads, soups, rice dishes and snacks.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Dried shrimp retain up to 80 % of their protein content after drying.
In Japan they are called “ebi-no-kashi” and are used in traditional broths.
Drying is performed in shade or specialized drying chambers to preserve flavor.
Shrimp are a marine “superfood” rich in trace minerals such as zinc and selenium.
In some countries dried shrimp are served as a seasoned snack.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Dried shrimp provide about 60 g of protein per 100 g, making them an excellent source of complete protein.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Unlike fresh shrimp, dried versions contain very little fat, suitable for calorie‑restricted diets.

items.title: Source of trace minerals
items.content: They contain zinc, selenium, iodine and iron, which support immune function and metabolism.

items.title: Contains omega‑3
items.content: Small amounts of omega‑3 fatty acids survive the drying process, benefiting heart health.

items.title: Supports bone health
items.content: Calcium and phosphorus present in dried shrimp contribute to bone strength.

items.title: Shellfish allergy
items.content: People allergic to shellfish may experience severe reactions to dried shrimp.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Dried shrimp are often salted; those monitoring sodium intake should limit portions.

items.title: Heavy‑metal contamination
items.content: Poor quality control can lead to traces of mercury or lead; purchase from reputable sources.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: Large amounts of dry shrimp can cause stomach upset in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Add dried shrimp to soups, ramen, salads, rice or noodle dishes, or use them as a fragrant garnish. Before use they are often re‑hydrated in warm water for 5‑10 minutes to soften.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from direct light. For long‑term storage, refrigerate or freeze to prevent oxidation and off‑flavors.
